board: Start of turn 4, all seven scoring cards still in the deck. The maintainer's stated calibration point, and the only turn at which a flat per-Battleground table is coherent: it is where the three Mid War regions stop being discounted and all six weigh the same.
unit: VP of total board-value swing from flipping one Battleground between the two sides. This is the quantity the maintainer prices in, and the one `scripts/position_pack.py` measures.
_floor_note: 'These BG countries are worth at least 4 VP each on turn 4 unscored.' The bot measures about 1.0 across the whole map.
_spread_note: Best Battleground minus worst, across the whole map. The bot's is 0.49.
_region_order_note: Ranked groups, best first; regions inside a group are not separated. All at turn 4 unscored, and Africa's fourth place is now the maintainer's word rather than an inference. The bot's measured order is AFRICA > SOUTH_AMERICA > CENTRAL_AMERICA > ASIA > EUROPE > MIDDLE_EAST.

urgency._note: The floor is real: `w.scoring_final * final_scoring_odds` survives every scoring card being played. The absolute level is NOT a parameter -- importance is `w.battleground * urgency` and `w.battleground` is free, so only the region-to-region and turn-to-turn ratios mean anything.

_structural: The ordering cannot be reached by tuning. `urgency` is built only from how soon and how often a region scores, with no term for what Control is worth on arrival, so Europe -- where Control ends the game -- can never outrank a region that scores more often. Europe's premium needs its own term.

control_efficiency._unit: Control VP divided by the summed stability of the region's Battlegrounds, i.e. what Control is worth over what it costs to take. Europe Control priced at 40.
control_efficiency._finding: Europe leads by 3.5x, which settles that its premium is structural. Below Europe the metric does NOT reproduce the maintainer's order -- it puts Africa second where they put it fourth and Central America third where they put it last, which is close to the bot's own wrong order. Efficiency measures the cost of taking and ignores the cost of keeping; Africa's 1-stability Battlegrounds are bought back for what they cost. Durability is the missing term, and it is the same one the wipe-exposure work arrived at.

tier_fit._unit: VP received at a tier against the average Ops of stability needed to reach it uncontested, 18 points over 3 tiers x 6 regions, Europe Control at its printed 7.
tier_fit._note: Near-linear. An earlier fit on MINIMUM Ops looked strongly concave (3.30*sqrt(Ops)); the maintainer corrected it to average Ops and the curvature vanished, because taking the cheapest country makes the low tiers look artificially cheap. Reconciles with the 2-Ops-per-VP rate: these are uncontested costs, so a contested game paying roughly double lands on the familiar rate.
tier_fit._europe: At its printed Control value Europe sits ON the curve like every other region (0.92x to 1.18x across all six). Its premium is entirely the automatic victory. Pricing Control at 40 is 3.6x the curve; the maintainer's figure for what it is worth to CHASE is about 1.67x, implying an effective Europe Control near 15 VP rather than 40.

Cuba.why: -1 VP for Fidel (wipes US Influence in Cuba outright) and -0.5 for Ortega, whose free Coup reaches Cuba because Cuba is adjacent to Nicaragua (verified in countries.json). Deck-conditional like every other per-country adjustment.

calibration_turn4._form: The maintainer's question -- 'what numbers line up with every BG being even except Europe and Thailand?' -- turns out to reproduce their own region ordering at the top with NO region weights at all. So the model is a flat base plus two exceptions plus a per-country table, not six region constants.
calibration_turn4._base_note: Every ordinary Battleground, their stated floor. The bot measures ~1.0.
calibration_turn4._europe_note: 'I really like that 6.5 number for Europe, but I could be off by a full VP' -- so 5.5 to 7.5. The only stated uncertainty band on any constant in this project, and worth more than the point estimate: it says a gate that moves Europe inside this range is not measuring anything.
calibration_turn4._thailand_note: Its Southeast Asia contribution on top of the ordinary Asia Battleground, giving 6.0. Not a multiplier: '1 + discounted scoring of 4 VP'.
calibration_turn4._africa_note: AMBIGUITY, and mine rather than theirs. 'Discount by maybe 2/3rds or 3/4ths' was read as multiply-by-0.3, which puts Africa LAST by a distance (mean 2.2-2.4) against their stated fourth. Read as multiply-by-0.67-0.75 it lands at 3.3-3.5, and 0.85 is what actually makes it fourth (3.64). Their 'still more valuable per Op' settles the direction: a 1-stability Battleground costs one Op against two, so at 0.7 it is still the better buy per Op, which is only true of the milder reading.
calibration_turn4._reconciliation: Top three exact: Europe, South America, Asia, in their order, from a flat base and two exceptions. The open question is Asia: it falls out at 3.83 where they place it second and separately suggested 'Asia at 5'. Asia's mean only reaches 5 with a base near 5.2, which would be a THIRD region exception and break the even-except-Europe-and-Thailand hypothesis they were testing. Either their second placement was loose, or Asia earns a premium its Domination 7 / Control 9 would justify. Not resolved.
